name: cannabis-biopesticide
description: In-silico biopesticide discovery from the Cannabis sativa (hemp) metabolome. Reproduces a denoised, docking-informed QSAR pipeline: molecular docking of ligands to 6 pest-relevant proteins (GluCl glutamate-gated chloride channel, AChE1 acetylcholinesterase, UGT202A2 and GSTM12 and agGSTe2 detoxification enzymes, OR28 odorant receptor), Mann-Whitney docking-score vs pesticide-activity analysis, Random Matrix Theory (Marchenko-Pastur) feature selection / denoising of residue-term docking energies, QSAR classification of pesticidal activity (DMPNN / gradient-boosting on RDKit descriptors, ROC-AUC ~0.93), applicability-domain filtering, and toxicity/ecotoxicity profiling. Reproduce the article as four separate scientific questions, beginning with canpest_dataset_overview; follow only each response's next_tools or terminal next_question transition, return the direct scientific answer and all non-null artifacts with URL/path, kind and SHA-256, and disclose metadata warnings. Use for: predicting biopesticide / insecticidal / acaricidal activity of plant secondary metabolites, terpenoids, cannabinoids, and natural products; docking-score analysis against insect/mite pest targets; RMT feature denoising of docking descriptors; virtual screening and hit prioritization of botanical insecticides; and looking up the paper's published natural-product vs synthetic-pesticide safety comparison (LD50, hepatotoxicity, aquatic ecotoxicity) as reference values. NOT an acute-toxicity server: it does not reproduce rodent LD50 / antitarget-panel toxicology (see tox-antitargets) and runs no live toxicity models (see heracleum-tox); its endpoint is pesticidal activity, not toxicity.
